title: Atollo — Universal Portable Dev & AI Workspace
description: An editor, 20+ languages, local databases and the Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity agents in one portable folder. Windows, macOS and Linux, x64 and ARM64. Zero install, zero admin rights.
heroTitle: Your sovereign dev & AI workspace, on any machine.
heroLead: Editor, runtimes, databases and AI agents. One portable folder across 6 targets.
heroZero: Zero install. Zero admin rights. Zero footprint outside your Atollo.
noRelease: No release published yet: the files arrive with the first tag.
metaphorText: An atoll is a ring of coral in the open ocean that encloses a calm, sheltered lagoon. The ocean is the host computer: a locked-down lab PC, a Mac, a Linux workstation full of clashing versions. The lagoon is the Atollo folder, with projects/ and data/: editor, languages, databases, GitHub account and AI agents live there, already set up, and when you eject the drive nothing is left on the PC.
f1Text: Built-in VSCodium with the Atollo dark and light themes. Terminals see only the kit's PATH and variables: programs on the host PC don't interfere, and the PC stays clean.
f2Text: 20+ languages and tools (Node.js, Python, uv, PHP, Rust, Go, Java, .NET, Dart, Julia, Ruby, C/C++, Bun, Deno, Typst, TinyTeX, R, Android SDK…), downloaded when needed and verified by SHA-256 checksum or signature. Side-by-side versions, one per project.
f3Text: MySQL with phpMyAdmin, MongoDB and SQLite, started and stopped with one click, with a database, user and password for each project. Caddy and Apache for sites. No system services.
f4Text: Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity: install, sign in and start. Write instructions, skills and MCP servers once in data/agents and atollo sync keeps all three aligned. Plan limits and usage for today and the last 7 days.
f5Text: The same folder, or the same external SSD, moves from Windows to macOS to Linux with projects, databases and agent settings intact: each machine runs the native programs of its system. “Remove drive” closes everything Atollo opened and lets you eject the disk.
how1: Copy Atollo into an empty folder: a USB stick, an external drive or a folder in your profile.
how2: Start it: it creates projects/ and data/. On first start choose agents, languages and tools; Atollo downloads and verifies them.
how3: Create or clone a project. The editor, terminal and agents always open in the project's folder.
c1Gap: Admin rights, Docker Desktop or WSL2; can't start from a USB stick on any PC.
c1Answer: Isolation without virtualization: native programs, no admin rights, starts from an external drive too.
c2Gap: Command line only; on Windows often needs WSL2; no editor, databases or agents.
c2Answer: Native GUI on Windows, macOS and Linux, with the editor, databases and agents built in.
c3Gap: One or two systems, mostly PHP and web, not portable from one system to another.
c3Answer: 20+ ecosystems and the same folder on 6 systems, with the AI agents.
c4Gap: Installed on the system, use global runtimes and make you configure MCP, skills and rules three times.
c4Answer: The editor and agents live in the kit, see the project's runtimes and share one configuration.
platformsLead: Windows 10 and 11, macOS 12 or later, Linux with glibc 2.35 or later (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and newer).
pWinArm: editor, PHP, Apache, MySQL and TinyTeX run under x64 emulation; no R
platformsNote: On macOS the app only has an ad hoc signature: after unzipping, remove the quarantine with xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine Atollo.app and open it from the kit folder. The macOS and Linux releases are tested in CI, not yet on clean machines.
privacyText: Atollo collects no data and contacts no server run by its author. It only connects to the official sources of the components you choose and, if you use them, to the GitHub and agent APIs.
footerSigning: Free code signing on Windows provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.
